chief_complaint: Management of cardiovascular risk factors and hypertension following prior myocardial infarction
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 57–year–old male with a history of an acute non‑ST‑segment elevation myocardial infarction in May 2017, for which he remains on secondary‑prevention therapy. Since then he has been treated for essential hypertension with a four‑drug regimen, metabolic syndrome, obesity, and pre‑diabetes (A1c 6.4%). He reports chronic pain, ongoing stress, unhealthy alcohol use, and a history of intimate‑partner abuse. Recent visits have focused on wellness and dental care; there are no recent lipid panels, renal function tests, or imaging studies to assess current disease control. Polypharmacy is moderate (seven agents) and several medication indications are undocumented.

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include primary dental caries (2024), gingivitis (2022), acute viral pharyngitis (2022), limited social contact (2020, 2021, 2023), prior part‑time/full‑time employment periods, and earlier episodes of stress that have resolved. The patient also has a longstanding background of higher education and past risk‑activity involvement. No chronic diseases have been documented as resolved.

BMI is missing despite documented obesity. Lipid panel, eGFR, and liver function are not available. Charlson comorbidity index is 1; clinical complexity is high. clinical_impression: A middle‑aged male with high cardiovascular risk due to prior MI, hypertension, metabolic syndrome, and obesity, maintained on an intensive secondary‑prevention regimen. Psychosocial stressors (alcohol misuse, chronic stress, intimate‑partner abuse) and chronic pain add complexity. Significant data gaps (BMI, lipid panel, renal and liver labs, cardiac imaging) limit precise risk stratification and optimization of therapy.
